To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the NIU heating plant manager was able to use the information and tools provided by the NIU faculty and student group to make a decision about the purchase of natural gas.

(a) the heating plant manager at NIU made a decision to ride the natural gas market during the 1997–98 heating season based on the information presented by the student group; (b) the manager's choice was a good one, because NIU saved $1.3 million in natural gas costs; and (c) the manager's decision was not based on ENSO information, but was rather influenced by the student group's presentation of local temperature forecasts.

the heating plant manager was willing to use climate information to aid in the decision process for the natural gas purchase, that a warmer-than-normal winter was forecasted, and that this forecast was correct.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a decision-making process that can be implemented to assist a weather-sensitive decision maker in making an annual decision to either ride the market or lock into a fixed-price contract for purchasing natural gas for heating purposes.
the development of a decision support system for the purchase of natural gas for a university heating plant.
how the weather-sensitive decision maker can incorporate climate information and forecast products to make better decisions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

there is a statistically significant positive correlation between the ENSO classification (El Nino, neutral, or La Nina) and the mean winter temperature in northern Illinois, and that the relationship is strongest when the ENSO is classified as an El Nino.
, in general, the NIU heating plant manager's decision to ride the market was a good one, but the decision to purchase natural gas in advance of the heating season was not.

the NIU heating plant manager's strategy of riding the market on a daily basis, based on the student group's ENSO information and forecast, was a successful one, and that the manager would likely continue this practice in the future.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NIU heating plant manager and his staff were willing to consider the use of seasonal climate information in their annual natural gas purchase strategy.
the ENSO phenomenon can provide useful information for a heating plant manager when making a fall natural gas purchasing decision.
we have demonstrated that the ENSO phenomenon can be used to predict winter temperature and, therefore, natural gas consumption in the Chicago region.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ENSO information was useful in the context of the decision process.
the heating plant manager was able to make a better decision by taking advantage of our climate forecast and analysis.
a university heating plant manager can benefit from using climate information and forecast models to assist with natural gas purchase decisions.
